Consult Summary:
- 45-year-old patient with 1 day of shortness of breath, pleuritic right-sided back pain, subjective fever, and two episodes of hemoptysis; on methotrexate for SLE; telehealth exam reassuring but plan for same-day in-person evaluation for suspected chest infection/pneumonia and vitals assessment.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Acute shortness of breath with pleuritic pain and hemoptysis.
- Symptom details:
  - Shortness of breath: Began today; associated with right-sided back pain that worsens with deep inspiration (pleuritic).
  - Hemoptysis: Coughed up blood on two occasions today.
  - Fever: Feels slightly febrile; temperature not measured (assessed with back of hand only).
  - Palpitations/awareness of heartbeat: Feels heart more than usual; unsure if faster; onset today.
  - Fatigue/reduced exercise tolerance: For “a couple of weeks,” difficulty exercising and performing daily activities.
- Timeline:
  - “Couple of weeks”: Fatigue, decreased exercise tolerance.
  - Today: Shortness of breath, pleuritic back pain (right), hemoptysis x2, subjective fever, awareness of heartbeat.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - Pain worsens with deep breathing.
- Associated symptoms:
  - No other specific associated symptoms documented.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No recent long-haul flights.
  - No personal history of DVT/PE.
  - No family history of blood clots.

Past Medical History:
- Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE)
  - On methotrexate.
  - No complications discussed.
- Medications:
  - Methotrexate (dose/route/frequency not documented); last taken this morning.
- Allergies:
  - No known drug allergies.
  - No other allergies reported.

Social History:
- Occupation: Office/desk job.
- Living situation: Lives alone in a flat.
- Pets: Cat.
- Tobacco: Does not smoke.
- Alcohol and other substances: Not documented.

Family History:
- No known family history of blood clots. Other family history not documented.

Physical Examination:
- Modality: Telehealth with limited remote assessment.
- General: Does not appear acutely unstable per clinician’s impression.
- Cardiovascular: Patient-counted radial pulse estimated by clinician at approximately 66–74 bpm.
- Perfusion: Capillary refill appeared normal on demonstration.
- Oropharynx: Visualized; no abnormalities documented.
- Lymph nodes: Patient self-palpation of cervical nodes; no enlargement felt.
- Vitals: No formal temperature, blood pressure, or oxygen saturation measured.

Investigations:
- None completed during this consult.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute cough with hemoptysis, pleuritic right-sided back pain, shortness of breath, subjective fever — likely chest infection/pneumonia; differentials include PE (risk factors denied: no long-haul flight, no personal/family VTE history) and less likely lung cancer given acute onset.
  - Plan:
    - Arrange same-day face-to-face clinic assessment.
    - Perform full vital signs: blood pressure, heart rate, temperature, oxygen saturation.
    - Chest examination with auscultation.
    - Consider chest X-ray if indicated and/or if symptoms do not settle.
    - Consider antibiotics based on in-person findings; no antibiotic prescribed now pending exam.
    - Safety net: chest infections can worsen; urgent care if symptoms escalate (worsening breathlessness, high fever, persistent/worsening hemoptysis, chest pain, dizziness, confusion).
    - Reassurance provided: acute presentation less suggestive of lung cancer; further investigations may be considered depending on exam and clinical course.
- Issue 2: Fatigue and reduced exercise tolerance for ~2 weeks.
  - Plan:
    - Evaluate during in-person visit; consider relation to current respiratory illness.
- Issue 3: SLE on methotrexate (immunosuppressed).
  - Plan:
    - Note immunosuppression when assessing infection severity and treatment.
    - No changes to methotrexate discussed today.

- General plan items:
  - Patient to call support team number (placed in appointment notes) to book same-day in-person GP review.
  - No medication allergies reported.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements:
  - Full vital signs (BP, temp, SpO2, RR) not obtained.
  - Comprehensive review of systems not performed/documented.
  - Methotrexate dose, route, and frequency not documented.
  - Immunization status, recent sick contacts, travel, and TB exposure not addressed.
● Internal conflicts:
  - Patient name provided as “Tracy Chapman” initially and later as “Doris” — conflict noted.
● Transcript quality:
  - Contains pauses/inaudible segments and some unclear statements; core clinical details present but limited by telehealth and audio quality.
